 Reporting from Washington
 Nov. 12, 2026 Updated 2:38 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. Encuentra más de nuestra cobertura en los resultados de búsqueda. Add The New York Times as a preferred source on Google Agrega The New York Times como fuente preferida en Google › 
 President Trump said on Thursday that he had pulled Vice President JD Vance back from engaging in potential peace talks with Iran, saying that his time would be better spent investigating fraud in Democratic-run jurisdictions.
 “We don’t need a deal with Iran,” Mr. Trump wrote on social media. “Those days have long since passed.”
 The post deepens questions about what Mr. Trump’s plan is to end the war. The president has been weighing a number of options, including ramping up military strikes, withdrawing and leaving the matter to Arab allies or simply maintaining the status quo.
 It also signals a pivot on his instructions to Mr. Vance, after the vice president publicly blamed the war for the Republican Party’s devastating midterm election losses in a striking critique of the administration’s agenda and messaging.
 Mr. Trump had assigned Mr. Vance, who privately expressed opposition to going to war with Iran, to lead negotiations earlier this year. The vice president traveled to Pakistan in April and met with Iranian leaders in a marathon session that ended without any resolution.
 Mr. Vance recently contacted a top Iranian political and military official to propose a renewal of comprehensive peace negotiations. In a letter sent from Mr. Vance via Qatari meditators to Gen. Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, the vice president suggested that American and Iranian officials meet soon, adding that he would lead the talks for the United States.
